# Beyond external aerodynamics {#sec-beyond-aero}

```{python}
#| label: setup-beyond
#| include: false
import json, statistics, math
from pathlib import Path
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
pct = lambda r: f"{abs(1 - r) * 100:.0f}%"
lead = lambda r: f"{(r - 1) * 100:.0f}%"
trail = lambda r: f"{(1 - r) * 100:.0f}%"
```

**Four datasets outside external aerodynamics exercise the parts of the
interface the aerodynamic sets leave idle, and ISLA leads GeoTransolver-512
where the target is a frame-free scalar and trails it where the target is a
stress tensor.** The four are a generated bracket family under prescribed
loads (DeepJEB++), two solids (PLAID Tensile2d, the GINOT bracket lug) and
two fixed-mesh problems whose boundary conditions are randomly placed and
labeled (the OLBC Poisson and elasticity sets); each is drawn on one sample
in @sec-datasets-beyond-aero and converted as @sec-datasets-detail records.
Protocol: @sec-protocol, float32, two seeds per cell, ISLA at the reference
configuration against the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512, and every
ratio is GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA, above one favoring ISLA.

## DeepJEB++ brackets: a load direction instead of a freestream {#sec-surface-deepjeb}

```{python}
#| label: setup-deepjeb
#| include: false
JB = J("deepjeb_2026-09-22.json"); JBS = JB["summary"]
JB_RUNGS = [("n256", 256, 500), ("n1024", 1024, 125), ("n4096", 4096, 32), ("full", 12451, 10)]
JB_FIELDS = [("von_mises", "von Mises stress"), ("displacement", "displacement")]
def jb_best(rung, f):
    """The GeoTransolver arm with the lowest mean on this rung and field, as the preregistration specifies."""
    cands = {a: JBS[f"{a}|{rung}"] for a in ("gt512", "gt512_lr3e3", "gt256") if f"{a}|{rung}" in JBS}
    a = min(cands, key=lambda a: cands[a]["fields"][f]["mean"]); return a, cands[a]
JB_NAME = {"gt512": "GeoTransolver-512 (1e-3)", "gt512_lr3e3": "GeoTransolver-512 (3e-3)", "gt256": "GeoTransolver-256 (1e-3)"}
jb_ratio = {(rung, f): jb_best(rung, f)[1]["fields"][f]["mean"] / JBS[f"isla_r1|{rung}"]["fields"][f]["mean"]
            for rung, _, _ in JB_RUNGS for f, _ in JB_FIELDS}
```

```{python}
#| label: para-deepjeb-lede
#| output: asis
vm = [jb_ratio[(r, "von_mises")] for r, _, _ in JB_RUNGS]; dp = [jb_ratio[(r, "displacement")] for r, _, _ in JB_RUNGS]
print(f"**On DeepJEB++, a surface task whose global vector is a load direction rather than a freestream, ISLA leads or ties the best "
      f"GeoTransolver arm at every rung of an equal-step ladder on both fields: GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA {min(vm):.2f} to {max(vm):.2f} on von "
      f"Mises stress and {min(dp):.2f} to {max(dp):.2f} on displacement over 256 to 12,451 training brackets.** DeepJEB++ "
      "(@sec-datasets-beyond-aero) is a family of generated jet-engine brackets. Each is solved by linear static finite elements under four "
      "load cases applied at the lug bore with the bolt holes clamped: three force directions and a torque about the lug axis. The "
      "surface mesh carries the fixed and loaded labels and the traction as boundary scalars. The load direction enters ISLA as the one "
      "global vector, and a force/torque one-hot enters as two global scalars (a moment axis is a pseudovector, so the model is told when the "
      "vector is an axis). The targets are von Mises stress and displacement at the surface cells. The test set is 1,385 held-out "
      "brackets under all four loads (5,540 files), scored in float32 over every surface cell. The ladder holds the optimizer-step "
      "budget fixed at about 130,000 steps while the training set grows (500, 125, 32 and 10 epochs at 256, 1,024, 4,096 and 12,451 "
      "brackets). It is therefore an equal-compute comparison at each rung and not a learning curve. Both architectures are flat above 1,024 "
      "brackets at this budget, which says the models are step-limited there, and the data exponent is not readable from it "
      "and the data exponent is not readable from it.")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-deepjeb-surface
#| output: asis
def jbcell(g, f):
    s = g["fields"][f]["seeds"]
    return f"{g['fields'][f]['mean']:.3f}" + (" (one seed)" if len(s) == 1 else "")
out = "| training brackets (epochs) | ISLA: von Mises / displacement | best GeoTransolver arm | its von Mises / displacement | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA |\n|---:|---|---|---|---:|\n"
for rung, n, ep in JB_RUNGS:
    i = JBS[f"isla_r1|{rung}"]
    a_vm, g_vm = jb_best(rung, "von_mises"); a_dp, g_dp = jb_best(rung, "displacement")
    arm = JB_NAME[a_vm] if a_vm == a_dp else f"{JB_NAME[a_vm]} / {JB_NAME[a_dp]}"
    out += (f"| {n:,} ({ep}) | {jbcell(i, 'von_mises')} / {jbcell(i, 'displacement')} | {arm} | {jbcell(g_vm, 'von_mises')} / "
            f"{jbcell(g_dp, 'displacement')} | {jb_ratio[(rung, 'von_mises')]:.2f} / {jb_ratio[(rung, 'displacement')]:.2f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": DeepJEB++ at equal optimizer steps (about 130,000; epochs in parentheses): relative L2 of von Mises stress and displacement over "
      "every surface cell, mean over the 5,540 clean test files, float32, two seeds unless marked. ISLA is the reference configuration "
      "(384 x 12, 5e-4, the load direction as the global vector); the GeoTransolver column is the arm with the lowest mean on that rung "
      "and field, as preregistered, among GeoTransolver-512 at 1e-3 and 3e-3 and GeoTransolver-256 at 1e-3 where they were run. How to read "
      "this: the ratio is GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA, above one favoring ISLA. The rows are equal-compute standings, not a learning curve, and the "
      "flatness above 1,024 brackets is the step budget. Data: results/deepjeb_2026-09-22.json; the notebook table of the same numbers is "
      "@tbl-deepjeb-equalstep. {#tbl-deepjeb-surface}")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-deepjeb-reading
#| output: asis
g512f = JBS["gt512|full"]["fields"]["von_mises"]["mean"]; g256f = JBS["gt256|full"]["fields"]["von_mises"]["mean"]
g3 = JBS["gt512_lr3e3|full"]["fields"]["von_mises"]["mean"]; g1 = JBS["gt512|full"]["fields"]["von_mises"]["mean"]
print(f"**Two things qualify every row of @tbl-deepjeb-surface.** Absolute errors are high for every model, a von Mises relative L2 near "
      f"0.5, and that is the dataset: a census of the labels found unphysical stress maxima on a tenth of the brackets, and the clean split "
      f"used here removes those without making the remaining stress fields smooth. And the ladder holds optimizer steps fixed rather than "
      f"epochs, so the flatness above 1,024 brackets is the step budget; at this budget the wider GeoTransolver-512 converges more slowly "
      f"({(g512f / g256f - 1) * 100:.0f}% behind 256 wide on von Mises) and the 3e-3 rate the surface protocol uses on the cars is "
      f"{(g3 / g1 - 1) * 100:.0f}% worse than 1e-3 here. Every row is an equal-compute standing, never a learning curve.")
```

## A solid: PLAID Tensile2d {#sec-interior-tensile2d}

```{python}
#| label: setup-tensile2d
#| include: false
SF = J("solids_frame_2026-09-22.json"); SFS = SF["summary"]
LM = J("lane_means_2026-09-23.json")  # per-lane float32 means; the tensor-head lanes with the load direction as the one global vector
T2D_FIELDS = [("sig11", "$\\sigma_{11}$"), ("sig22", "$\\sigma_{22}$"), ("sig12", "$\\sigma_{12}$"), ("displacement", "displacement")]
T2D_RUNGS = (32, 400)
def t2_isla(n):
    runs = [LM[f"v2_t2d_isla_r1_tensor_axis_n{n}_seed{s}"]["fields"] for s in (42, 43)]
    return {f: dict(mean=statistics.mean(r[f] for r in runs), seeds=[r[f] for r in runs]) for f, _ in T2D_FIELDS}
def t2_gt(n):
    d = SFS[f"gt512|gt|n{n}"]["fields"]
    return {f: dict(mean=d[f]["mean"], seeds=d[f].get("seeds", [])) for f, _ in T2D_FIELDS}
T2I = {n: t2_isla(n) for n in T2D_RUNGS}; T2G = {n: t2_gt(n) for n in T2D_RUNGS}
T2R = {n: {f: T2G[n][f]["mean"] / T2I[n][f]["mean"] for f, _ in T2D_FIELDS} for n in T2D_RUNGS}
import math
slope = lambda arm, f: math.log(arm[32][f]["mean"] / arm[400][f]["mean"]) / math.log(400 / 32)
r400 = T2R[400]
```

```{python}
#| label: tensile2d-lede
#| output: asis
print(f"**On the first solid-mechanics dataset, PLAID Tensile2d, GeoTransolver-512 leads ISLA at "
      f"400 training cases by {trail(r400['sig11'])} on $\\sigma_{{11}}$, {trail(r400['sig22'])} on $\\sigma_{{22}}$, "
      f"{trail(r400['sig12'])} on $\\sigma_{{12}}$ and {trail(r400['displacement'])} on the displacement; between 32 and 400 cases "
      f"ISLA's error falls faster on every field (two-point slopes {slope(T2I, 'sig11'):.2f} against {slope(T2G, 'sig11'):.2f} on "
      f"$\\sigma_{{11}}$), so the gap narrows with data and is the open standing on the solids.** "
      f"Tensile2d (@sec-data-tensile2d) is two-dimensional elasto-viscoplastic tension: per case a load $P$ on the top "
      f"edge and five constitutive scalars vary, the geometry barely does, and the targets are the displacement and the "
      f"three in-plane stress components. Every mesh node is an interacting query token; ISLA reads the boundary polyline "
      f"with its condition labels, receives the load direction as its one global vector and the six scalars, and predicts "
      f"the stress as a symmetric tensor whose components the recipe reads off (@sec-isla-heads); GeoTransolver reads every "
      f"node with the nodal condition tags in its local embedding. Both models use the reference configurations (ISLA at "
      f"384 x 12; GeoTransolver-512, its parameter match).")
```

```{python}
#| label: tensile2d-ladder-table
#| output: asis
def tcell(d): return f"{d['mean']:.4f}" + (f" ({' / '.join(f'{v:.4f}' for v in d['seeds'])})" if d["seeds"] else "")
hdr = "| training cases | " + " | ".join(f"ISLA {l} | GeoTransolver {l} | ratio" for _, l in T2D_FIELDS) + " |"
print(hdr); print("|" + "---|" * (1 + 3 * len(T2D_FIELDS)))
for n in T2D_RUNGS:
    print(f"| {n} | " + " | ".join(f"{tcell(T2I[n][f])} | {tcell(T2G[n][f])} | {T2R[n][f]:.2f}" for f, _ in T2D_FIELDS) + " |")
print("| two-point slope, 32 to 400 | " + " | ".join(f"{slope(T2I, f):.2f} | {slope(T2G, f):.2f} | " for f, _ in T2D_FIELDS) + " |")
print()
print(": PLAID Tensile2d, float32 relative L2 on the 100 held-out cases at 500 epochs (mean of two seeds; seeds in parentheses), ISLA "
      "with the tensor head and the load direction as its one global vector against GeoTransolver-512, at 32 and 400 training cases; "
      "the last row is the learning-curve slope between the two rungs (error proportional to cases to the minus alpha). How to read "
      "this: a ratio below one is a GeoTransolver lead; only two rungs exist under this configuration, so the slope is a two-point "
      "estimate and not a fitted exponent. The five-rung ladder measured earlier used the dataset's axes as global vectors, an input "
      "the book rejects; it is reported only as the pose-prior diagnostic of @sec-pose-prior. Data: results/lane_means_2026-09-23.json "
      "(ISLA); results/solids_frame_2026-09-22.json (GeoTransolver-512). {#tbl-tensile2d-ladder}")
```

This table measures two things and does not measure a third. It measures
the standing of the general interface on a problem with one global
direction, the load, and six global scalars: a 1.3x to 2x GeoTransolver
lead at 400 cases, the direction the preregistration predicted. It measures the learning-curve slope between
the two rungs, steeper for ISLA on every field, the same ordering as the
AirfRANS ladder (@sec-interior-airfrans) and the DrivAerML law
(@sec-compute-allocation). It does not measure geometry generalization or
discretization invariance, since the specimen shape hardly varies and each
case has one mesh. Those axes stay with the aerodynamic datasets. This is
the dataset on which the component clause of the output contract binds: a
scalar-head configuration with no direction at all fits the training set
and memorizes it, validating 20 to 60 times worse than GeoTransolver,
because a stress component is a view of a tensor and not a channel
(@sec-isla-heads). The 24-layer depth variant is 9% to 27% *worse* than 12
layers at 400 cases on every field, so depth does not pay on Tensile2d at
this data size.

## A second solid: the GINOT bracket lug {#sec-interior-lug}

```{python}
#| label: setup-lug
#| include: false
LUG = J("solids_lug_2026-09-22.json"); LUGS = LUG["summary"]; LUGR = LUG["gt512_over_isla"]; LUGX = LUG["learning_curve_exponents"]
LUG_RUNGS = (300, 600, 1200, 2400)
# the 300-lug rung is reported at the half rate (2.5e-4), the rerun the preregistration prescribes for a lane that sat on a plateau;
# the 5e-4 lane at 300 lugs is shown beside it
lug_isla = {300: LUGS["isla_r1_lr25e4|n300"], 600: LUGS["isla_r1|n600"], 1200: LUGS["isla_r1|n1200"], 2400: LUGS["isla_r1|n2400"]}
lug_ratio = {300: LUGR["isla_r1_lr25e4|n300"], 600: LUGR["isla_r1|n600"], 1200: LUGR["isla_r1|n1200"], 2400: LUGR["isla_r1|n2400"]}
```

```{python}
#| label: lug-lede
#| output: asis
print(f"**On the GINOT bracket lug, a three-dimensional elastoplastic solid whose target is a true scalar (von Mises stress) and whose load "
      f"is a pressure on the hole with no global direction, ISLA leads GeoTransolver-512 at the two small rungs of the training-case ladder and ties at the two large ones: "
      f"GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA {lug_ratio[300]:.2f} / {lug_ratio[600]:.2f} / {lug_ratio[1200]:.2f} / {lug_ratio[2400]:.2f} "
      f"at 300 / 600 / 1,200 / 2,400 lugs, with learning-curve exponents {LUGX['isla_r1']['exponent']:.2f} against "
      f"{LUGX['gt512']['exponent']:.2f}.** The lug (@sec-data-lug) is clamped at one end and pressed on the lower half of its hole; three "
      "geometry parameters and the pressure vary, and the target is the nodal von Mises stress. ISLA reads the boundary triangles with the "
      "clamped, hole, loaded and pressure labels as boundary scalars, the four design parameters as global scalars, and every node as a "
      "query with its signed distance ($K = 0$: no global vector); GeoTransolver-512 reads every node with the nodal tags and the "
      "parameters in its global embedding. The 600 test lugs are scored in float32 at every node.")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-lug-ladder
#| output: asis
def lcell(g): return f"{g['mean']:.4f} ({' / '.join(f'{v:.4f}' for v in g['seeds'])})" + (" (one seed)" if len(g["seeds"]) == 1 else "")
out = "| training lugs | ISLA (rate) | GeoTransolver-512 (1e-3) | GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA |\n|---:|---|---|---:|\n"
for n in LUG_RUNGS:
    rate = "2.5e-4, the half-rate rerun" if n == 300 else "5e-4"
    out += f"| {n:,} | {lcell(lug_isla[n])} ({rate}) | {lcell(LUGS[f'gt512|n{n}'])} | {lug_ratio[n]:.2f} |\n"
out += f"| 300, the 5e-4 lane | {lcell(LUGS['isla_r1|n300'])} (5e-4; seed 42 escaped a plateau late) | {lcell(LUGS['gt512|n300'])} | {LUGR['isla_r1|n300']:.2f} |\n"
out += f"| exponent, 300 to 2,400 | {LUGX['isla_r1']['exponent']:.2f} | {LUGX['gt512']['exponent']:.2f} | |\n"
print(out)
print(": GINOT bracket lug: relative L2 of von Mises stress over the 600 test lugs (mean over lugs, then over seeds; seeds in parentheses), "
      "float32 at every node, 500 epochs, ISLA at the reference configuration against GeoTransolver-512, its parameter match. The 300-lug "
      "row is reported at 2.5e-4; at 5e-4 one seed did not train, and that lane is the row below. "
      "The exponent is the least-squares learning-curve exponent over the "
      "four rungs, ISLA's from the half-rate 300-lug value. How to read this: a ratio above one is an ISLA lead; the 2,400-lug ISLA cell "
      "holds one scored seed in the artifact. Data: results/solids_lug_2026-09-22.json. {#tbl-lug-ladder}")
```

The lug and Tensile2d pull in opposite directions on the standing and the
same direction on the learning curve. Tensile2d's targets are the
components of a stress tensor, which ISLA predicts as a tensor
(@sec-isla-heads), and GeoTransolver-512 leads there at 400 cases. The
lug's target is a frame-free scalar and its loading has no direction of
its own, and ISLA leads. On both, ISLA's error falls faster with cases
than GeoTransolver-512's. The largest lug rung carries one scored ISLA
seed, which the table says, and no width or depth control.

## Boundary data on a fixed mesh: the OLBC sets {#sec-interior-olbc}

```{python}
#| label: setup-olbc
#| include: false
# Every OLBC number below is read from one consolidated artifact: ISLA at the reference configuration with no option,
# and GeoTransolver-512 with both of its released attention backends.
OLB = J("olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json"); OLP = OLB["poisson"]; OLE = OLB["elasticity"]
OL_RUNGS = (512, 2048, 8448)
PF = "u_l2"
OL_EL = [("displacement_l2", "displacement"), ("sig11_l2", "$\\sigma_{11}$"), ("sig22_l2", "$\\sigma_{22}$"), ("sig12_l2", "$\\sigma_{12}$")]
EL_STRESS = [f for f, _ in OL_EL if f != "displacement_l2"]
BACKEND = {"physics": "physics attention", "flarepp": "FLARE++"}
seeds_of = lambda cell, f: [cell["per_seed"][s][f] for s in sorted(cell["per_seed"])]
def num(cell, f, nd=4):
    return f"{cell['means'][f]:.{nd}f} ({' / '.join(f'{v:.{nd}f}' for v in seeds_of(cell, f))})"
gt_ratio = lambda rung, backend, f: rung["gt512_over_isla"][backend]["ratio"][f]
fmt_ratio = lambda x, nd=2: f"{x:.{nd}f}"
stronger = lambda rung: rung["stronger_gt512"]
def headline(rung, f):
    """GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA against the stronger backend at that rung, with the backend name."""
    b = stronger(rung); return gt_ratio(rung, b, f), BACKEND[b]
def span(vals, nd=2):
    return f"{min(vals):.{nd}f} to {max(vals):.{nd}f}"
P_HEAD = {n: headline(OLP[str(n)], PF) for n in OL_RUNGS}
E_STRESS = {n: span([gt_ratio(OLE[str(n)], stronger(OLE[str(n)]), f) for f in EL_STRESS]) for n in OL_RUNGS}
E_DISP = {n: fmt_ratio(gt_ratio(OLE[str(n)], stronger(OLE[str(n)]), "displacement_l2")) for n in OL_RUNGS}
ol_exp = lambda means: math.log(means[0] / means[-1]) / math.log(8448 / 512)
```

```{python}
#| label: olbc-lede
#| output: asis
print(f"**On the OLBC sets, where one fixed mesh per set carries a boundary cut per sample into random labeled Dirichlet, Neumann and "
      f"Robin segments, ISLA with no option leads GeoTransolver-512 on the scalar Poisson set at the two small rungs "
      f"(GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA {fmt_ratio(P_HEAD[512][0])} at 512 cases and {fmt_ratio(P_HEAD[2048][0])} at 2,048) and trails it at "
      f"8,448 ({fmt_ratio(P_HEAD[8448][0])}), and trails it on the elasticity tensor at every rung, by {E_STRESS[8448]} on the stresses and "
      f"{E_DISP[8448]} on displacement at 8,448 cases.** These sets (@sec-data-olbc) are the complement of every other dataset in the book: "
      "the geometry never varies and only the boundary data do, so the task is the pure boundary-data-to-solution map on a known domain. "
      "The ladders are @tbl-olbc-ladder; the backend each ratio is taken against is named there, because GeoTransolver's two released "
      "attention backends cross between the rungs on the Poisson set.")
```

On the Poisson set ($-\nabla^2 u = f$ on a square, with a random
sinusoidal source and four random boundary segments per sample) ISLA reads
the boundary segments with the condition type and value as boundary
scalars and every node as a query, and the problem has no global vector
($K = 0$). On the elasticity set (steel, a disc with two holes, a
prescribed displacement and tractions per component) it receives the
prescribed displacement and traction as rank-1 boundary inputs and
predicts the stress as a symmetric tensor (@sec-isla-inputs-rank).
GeoTransolver-512 reads every node with the nodal condition tags. The 256
test samples of each set are scored in float32 at every node, two seeds per
cell; the 512- and 2,048-case rungs train for 500 epochs and the
8,448-case rung for 120, the same optimizer-step count as 2,048 cases at
500, which is a stated deviation from the protocol and applies to both
architectures alike.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-olbc-ladder
#| output: asis
def gt_cell(rung, backend, f, nd=4):
    cell = rung[f"gt512_{backend}"]; txt = num(cell, f, nd)
    return f"**{txt}** (stronger)" if stronger(rung) == backend else txt
out = ("| OLBC Poisson, training cases | ISLA $u$ | GeoTransolver-512 $u$, physics attention | GeoTransolver-512 $u$, FLARE++ | "
       "GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA (stronger backend) |\n|---:|---|---|---|---:|\n")
for n in OL_RUNGS:
    r = OLP[str(n)]; h = P_HEAD[n]
    out += (f"| {n:,} | {num(r['reference'], PF)} | {gt_cell(r, 'physics', PF)} | {gt_cell(r, 'flarepp', PF)} | "
            f"{fmt_ratio(h[0])} ({h[1]}) |\n")
g256 = OLP["8448"].get("gt256_physics")
if g256 and "means" in g256:
    out += (f"| 8,448, GeoTransolver-256 (physics attention) | | {num(g256, PF)} | | "
            f"{fmt_ratio(g256['means'][PF] / OLP['8448']['reference']['means'][PF])} |\n")
isla_p = [OLP[str(n)]["reference"]["means"][PF] for n in OL_RUNGS]
gt_p = [OLP[str(n)][f"gt512_{stronger(OLP[str(n)])}"]["means"][PF] for n in OL_RUNGS]
out += f"| learning-curve exponent, 512 to 8,448 | {ol_exp(isla_p):.2f} | | | {ol_exp(gt_p):.2f} (GeoTransolver-512) |\n"
out += ("\n| OLBC elasticity, training cases, field | ISLA | GeoTransolver-512, physics attention | GeoTransolver-512, FLARE++ | "
        "GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA (stronger backend) |\n|---|---|---|---|---:|\n")
for n in OL_RUNGS:
    r = OLE[str(n)]; b = stronger(r)
    for f, lab in OL_EL:
        out += (f"| {n:,}, {lab} | {num(r['reference'], f, 3)} | {gt_cell(r, 'physics', f, 3)} | {gt_cell(r, 'flarepp', f, 3)} | "
                f"{fmt_ratio(gt_ratio(r, b, f))} ({BACKEND[b]}) |\n")
print(out)
print(": The OLBC ladders: relative L2 over the 256 test samples of each set (mean over samples, then over seeds; seeds in parentheses), "
      "float32 at every node, two seeds per cell. ISLA is the reference configuration with no option; GeoTransolver-512 is scored with both "
      "of its released attention backends, and **the ratio column is GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA against the stronger backend at that rung**, "
      "which is marked in bold and named beside the ratio. Top: the Poisson set's solution $u$ along the 512 / 2,048 / 8,448-case ladder, "
      "with GeoTransolver-256 at the full rung, and the learning-curve exponent of each architecture's total error over the ladder. Bottom: "
      "the elasticity set per field, ISLA with the prescribed displacement and traction as rank-1 boundary inputs and the stress as a tensor "
      "output. How to read this: a ratio above one is an ISLA lead and below one a GeoTransolver-512 lead; the two backends are never "
      "averaged, and a ratio against the weaker backend is never the headline. The 8,448-case rung trains for 120 epochs rather than 500 "
      "for both architectures, so it is an equal-step rung and its exponent is a compute statement as much as a data one. "
      "Data: results/olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json. {#tbl-olbc-ladder}")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-olbc-reading
#| output: asis
print(f"**The Poisson lead is a small-data lead: GeoTransolver-512's error falls faster along the ladder ("
      f"exponent {ol_exp(gt_p):.2f} against ISLA's {ol_exp(isla_p):.2f}) and it overtakes between 2,048 and 8,448 cases.** The elasticity "
      f"ordering does not move with data: GeoTransolver-512 leads on every field at every rung, by {E_STRESS[512]} on the stresses at 512 "
      f"cases and {E_STRESS[8448]} at 8,448. These two sets are the one place in the book where the geometry carries no information at all, "
      "so what separates the architectures here is how each reads per-cell boundary data, and the elasticity set is the harder test because "
      "its boundary data are rank-1 and its target a tensor. Per-type geometry channels added to ISLA on these meshes are neutral or worse "
      "and are not part of the model (@sec-olbc-ablations).")
```

## What the general interface buys here, and where it trails {#sec-beyond-standing}

```{python}
#| label: para-beyond-open
#| output: asis
print(f"**One interface covers four problems outside external aerodynamics, and the standings split by target rather than by physics: "
      f"ISLA leads where the target is a frame-free scalar and trails where it is a tensor.** On the GINOT lug's von Mises stress it "
      f"leads GeoTransolver-512 at the two small rungs and ties at the two large ones (GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA {lug_ratio[2400]:.2f} at "
      f"2,400 lugs) with the steeper learning curve; on DeepJEB++ it leads or ties the best GeoTransolver arm at every rung of an "
      f"equal-step ladder; and on the scalar OLBC Poisson set it leads at 512 and 2,048 cases with no option "
      f"({fmt_ratio(P_HEAD[512][0])} and {fmt_ratio(P_HEAD[2048][0])}) before GeoTransolver-512 overtakes at 8,448 "
      f"({fmt_ratio(P_HEAD[8448][0])}). On PLAID Tensile2d's stress tensor GeoTransolver-512 leads at 400 cases, and on the OLBC "
      f"elasticity set it leads on every field at every rung, by {E_STRESS[8448]} on the stresses and {E_DISP[8448]} on displacement at "
      f"8,448 cases. The two tensor-target solids are the open standings of this chapter and the ones that most need a located mechanism; "
      "the limits of all of them are collected in @sec-limits-datasets. "
      "Data: results/deepjeb_2026-09-22.json; results/lane_means_2026-09-23.json; results/solids_frame_2026-09-22.json; "
      "results/solids_lug_2026-09-22.json; results/olbc_ref_2026-09-29.json.")
```
